title: The Educated Barbarian: Hagakure analysis (part. 7)
summary: NH continues his Hagakure commentary: peripheral vision, 'dog's skin inside, tiger's hide outside', pure will as the key to training, finding and keeping a passion, and copying versus building your own archetype. He ties each to bodybuilding, keeping lifting pure and rejecting echo chambers.
claims: Seeing in one direction means seeing in all; peripheral awareness can save your life, echoing Musashi
The samurai should be like a dog inside, loyal, disciplined and routine-driven, and a tiger outside, fierce and indifferent to looks
Discipline is the ability to repeat the same thing again and again; that's how you get great
Your outward image need not reveal who you are, and hiding your true self can ward off bad influences
Looking powerful is being powerful: once you get big, people stop messing with you because predators seek weak prey
The most important thing in training is pure will in every moment; it can be encouraged but not taught
His will came the day he decided he couldn't keep living as he was, and it never left
Everyone who succeeds in bodybuilding has that will and must strengthen it like steel
Today's fitness crowd wants quick fixes and magic programs because they lack will; with will, rocks, sticks and a tree build a big body
He realized he loved bodybuilding around 20-21, but always preferred weight training over sport practices since doing push-ups and curls as a small kid
Passion is hard to hold because life responsibilities pull you away; falling out of love with a hobby is heartbreaking
His trigger for losing passion would be bodybuilding becoming a job, so he refuses to make money from it to keep it pure
Start now; don't put things off until tomorrow
Copying a model is necessary as a beginner, but never try to become or idolize that person
Teachers deserve respect but not reverence; their only advantage is years and their goal should be to be surpassed
You can only recognize virtues in others that you already carry within you
He never agrees 100% with anyone but himself; disagreement creates discussion while agreement-only circles are fake positivity and echo chambers
Seek out conflicting ideas to oppose yours, as long as egos stay out of the debate
Negativity is a natural, important part of life; fake positivity is what we can do without
